propositions: On platforms without /proc, _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant in _mkdir_lock_is_stale unsatisfiable and causing unbounded lock wedging when a dead process's pid is reused by an unrelated live process
When current_start is None (unavailable), the live-pid verdict becomes unqualified and must fall back to the 1h ceiling backstop rather than treating a bare pid collision as liveness proof

A genuinely live owner inside its hold retains the exclusive fcntl leg for the entire mkdir lock lifetime, so reaching the stale-check ceiling is itself evidence of orphan ownership and safe to reclaim
The fix splits lock.py (798/800 LOC) into lock.py and lock_owner.py along the call-graph seam of the owner-identity/stamp/staleness/reclaim cluster to satisfy the hard module-size limit
All 12 monkeypatch string-form sites and 42 attribute-access sites in test modules must be repointed to lock_owner with no re-export shim to preserve patch semantics
